newsitem.title: SYRIA: France, Syria sign debt deal, details withheld.
newsitem.headline: France, Syria sign debt deal, details withheld.

text.p: France and Syria signed an agreement on Sunday on a dispute over Syria's debt to Paris, opening the way for an expansion of economic relations, President Jacques Chirac announced.

But he did not say how much of the 1.8 billion franc ($350 million) debt was being forgiven, rescheduled or refinanced at lower interest rates, and specialist French ministers doggedly refused to disclose the figures.
Chirac said the ministers had put an end to a decade-old dispute that had stopped French financial aid and export credit guarantees to Damascus.
Under the agreement, the French Treasury would make available fresh funds for economic projects, Chirac said. French officials said the sum involved was 138 million francs.
Syrian sources said Damascus would end up reimburing 1.1 billion francs over time, with the remaining 700 million francs converted into contracts.
French officials said the debt consisted of 800 million francs in principal and interest, and one billion francs in arrears since 1987, when Damascus stopped paying.
Chirac said France would support Syria's case in international financial instituions and ensure it got a good share of European Union funds for Mediterranean basin projects.
Chirac and President Hafez al-Assad held an unscheduled extra session of talks on Sunday night to discuss new bilateral economic and cultural projects following the debt deal, the officials said.
